_comment: IOC feed for bluehammer_defender_audit. All indicators are transcribed from the Huntress 'nightmare-eclipse-intrusion' analysis (source_url), each with a citation. IMPORTANT: Huntress published NO file hash for the BlueHammer binary itself (FunnyApp.exe). The only hash available is for BeigeBurrow, the co-occurring tunnel agent, and is labelled as such below. No BlueHammer hash is fabricated. The module matches on path_regexes and file_hashes_sha256; the c2/source_ips fields are network context for the writeup and are NOT matched by the module.

path_regexes.desc: lone EXE in a nested subfolder under a user's Pictures dir (BlueHammer drop pattern)
lone EXE in a nested subfolder under a user's Downloads dir (observed drop pattern)
observed BlueHammer filename (low confidence - trivially renamed)
observed RedSun filename (associated tooling; low confidence)
observed UnDefend filename (associated tooling; low confidence)

file_hashes_sha256.desc: BeigeBurrow tunnel agent - ASSOCIATED tooling from the same intrusion, NOT the BlueHammer binary

c2.desc: BeigeBurrow C2 destination (network context; not matched by the module)
